title: Prefix Sums
tagline: Precompute running totals once; answer any range-sum query in O(1).

intuition.analogy: A bank statement lists your running balance after every transaction. To know how much you spent between Tuesday and Friday, you don't re-add every purchase — you subtract Tuesday's balance from Friday's. The running balance is a prefix sum.
paragraphs: If you'll be asked many 'sum of elements from i to j' questions, recomputing each from scratch is O(n) per query. Prefix sums pay O(n) once to precompute cumulative totals, after which any range sum is a single subtraction.
Define pre[k] = a[0] + a[1] + … + a[k-1] (with pre[0] = 0). Then the sum of a[l..r] equals pre[r+1] - pre[l]. The off-by-one is tamed by the extra leading zero.

The idea generalises: prefix XOR, prefix products, 2D prefix sums for submatrix queries, and — most powerfully — combining prefix sums with a hash map to count subarrays whose sum equals a target in O(n).
intuition.keyIdea: Range sum [l, r] = pre[r+1] − pre[l]. Precompute once, query forever in O(1).

steps.title: Build the prefix array
steps.detail: pre[0] = 0; for i from 1 to n, pre[i] = pre[i-1] + a[i-1]. The leading zero makes range math clean.

steps.title: Answer queries
steps.detail: Sum of a[l..r] = pre[r+1] − pre[l]. Constant time per query.

steps.title: Hash-map extension
steps.detail: To count subarrays with sum = k, walk prefix sums and look up how many earlier prefixes equal current − k.

codes.title: subarray_sum_equals_k.cpp
subarray_sum_equals_k.py
codes.source:
def subarray_sum(nums, k):
    count = 0
    prefix = 0
    seen = {0: 1}                 # empty prefix
    for x in nums:
        prefix += x
        count += seen.get(prefix - k, 0)
        seen[prefix] = seen.get(prefix, 0) + 1
    return count

complexity.time: O(n) build, O(1) per range query
complexity.timeReason: One linear pass builds the array; each query is one subtraction.
complexity.spaceReason: Stores the prefix array (or hash map of seen prefixes).

pitfalls: Off-by-one: with pre[0]=0, the range [l, r] uses pre[r+1] − pre[l], not pre[r] − pre[l].
For the hash-map count trick, seed the map with {0: 1} to count subarrays starting at index 0.
Watch for integer overflow with large arrays — use 64-bit sums.

rows: Range [2,5] uses indices r+1=6 and l=2
dryRun.clickMoment: The single subtraction pre[6] − pre[2] replaced summing four elements. With a thousand queries, that's the difference between O(1000·n) and O(n + 1000).
